title.narrative: Percentage of beneficiaries that feel project activities reflected their needs (Citizen Engagement indicator)

comment.narrative:
91% is from the PFIs evaluations as well as the independent training survey conducted by the M&E team of the Project. Survey which will be conducted by the firm is expected in Q3 2025.
This indicator measures the satisfaction of beneficiary MSMEs and PFIs. This indicator will measure the results of surveys conducted as part of the monitoring and evaluation strategy implemented during Project implementation to beneficiary MSMEs and PFIs about their satisfaction with the financial products offered under the Project. The survey results and the report will be shared by the PMU and will contain proposed recommendations for project adjustments. The PMU will, in turn, make the necessary adjustment to activities, as informed by citizen feedback.

title.narrative: Number of businesses supported with technical assistance

comment.narrative: With the project restructuring, this indicator will be revised down from 600 to 400. This takes into account the implementation delays as well as the decision by the MOIC to provide targeted training to select MSMEs thereby enhancing productivity outcomes. The performance is expected to improve following planned bootcamp training sessions during the proposed project extension period.

title.narrative: Number of MSMEs benefitting from TA that obtain credit

comment.narrative: This indicator measures number of MSMEs benefitting from TA from the project confirming that they obtain credit. The phrase “for the first time” will be removed with project restructuring to broaden the indicator's scope, capturing all MSMEs that access credit because of TA, whether for their initial loan or subsequent ones. Considering the time lost due to implementation delays, the indicator target is proposed to be revised down from 30 to 15 to reflect a more realistic and achievable goal within the remaining project period.

As of October 2025, 99 percent MSMEs benefitting from the line of credit reported to survive COVID-19 crisis.

title.narrative: TA to strengthen BOL capacity to supervise and monitor PCG delivered

comment.narrative: The project has delivered technical assistance to BOL to strengthen its capacity to supervise and monitor the PCG Fund. Several workshops have been delivered. In addtion, two study visits were conducted and supervision procedural documents developed. The international consultant has submitted drafts of legislation and guidelines. Legal framework for the establishment of LCGF need to be in place.

title.narrative: Percentage of complaints handled from Grievance Redress mechanism in place (disaggregated by number/percent of women)

comment.narrative: This indicator is on track to be achieved. The GRM is in place and 5 complaints have been received to date. In addition, a Booklet of guidelines that combine the Environmental Management, Work safety Measures, Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) for MSMEs in Lao Language was completed and submitted to National Management Committee on Unexploded Ordinance, and the Department of Natural Resources and Environment Inspection (DoNREI) for their review and comments on September 12, 2022. The DoNREI provided comments on September 19, 2022, which were addressed by DOSMEP on September 30, 2022. The revised booklet has been published and circulated to MSMEs.
